microtheory.name: cognitive_psychology
microtheory.definition: Cognitive psychology — the empirical study of internal mental processes: perception, attention, memory, language, reasoning, problem-solving, decision-making. The 'cognitive revolution' replaced behaviourism's reluctance to discuss internal states. Major figures: Neisser, Miller, Newell + Simon, Tversky + Kahneman, Anderson. Substrate analogue: most of the substrate's cortex + cortices implement cognitive psychology constructs directly.

concepts.name: working_memory_psychological
concepts.definition: Baddeley + Hitch 1974. Central executive + phonological loop + visuospatial sketchpad + (later) episodic buffer. Capacity 4±1 chunks (Cowan 2001) — revised from Miller's 7±2. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent σ across tick cycles.

concepts.name: long_term_memory_systems
concepts.definition: Tulving 1985: episodic (events), semantic (facts), procedural (skills), priming (implicit). Each has different brain substrates + retention curves. Substrate analogue: substrate's events vs concepts vs FilterSpec dispatch vs covered-by-* attrs.

concepts.name: encoding_specificity
concepts.definition: Tulving + Thomson 1973. Retrieval is best when context matches encoding context. State-dependent memory. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ pattern at recall must match the σ pattern at encoding.

concepts.name: levels_of_processing
concepts.definition: Craik + Lockhart 1972. Deeper (semantic) processing → better retention than shallow (surface). Substrate analogue: substrate's concept integration into existing Mt scaffolds vs orphan event nodes.

concepts.name: false_memory
concepts.definition: Roediger + McDermott 1995. Memories of events that didn't occur, reconstructed from gist + schema-based inference. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-completion in CA3-analogue producing plausible-but-false retrievals.

concepts.name: selective_attention
concepts.definition: Cherry 1953 cocktail party effect. Attention to one channel suppresses others. Broadbent's filter, Treisman's attenuation, Lavie's load theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's policy_filter selection.

concepts.name: divided_attention
concepts.definition: Trying to process multiple streams. Generally degrades performance. Strayer + Drews 2007 distracted driving. Substrate analogue: substrate's simultaneous Mt activations interfere unless they don't share concepts.

concepts.name: attentional_blink
concepts.definition: Raymond 1992. ~500ms after attending to T1, you miss T2. Attention has a temporal refractory period. Substrate analogue: substrate's tick-cycle limit on consecutive high-attention events.

concepts.name: change_blindness
concepts.definition: Failure to notice large changes when attention isn't focused on them. Simons + Levin 1998 door-swap. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-state stable across ticks unless attended.

concepts.name: inattentional_blindness
concepts.definition: Failure to perceive unexpected stimuli when attention is engaged elsewhere. Simons + Chabris 1999 gorilla. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime_discovery firing only configured handlers.

concepts.name: feature_integration_theory
concepts.definition: Treisman 1980. Separate features (color, shape, motion) are detected pre-attentively; binding into objects requires attention. Substrate analogue: substrate's gamma-band synchronisation analogue binds feature concepts into Assessment nodes.

concepts.name: gestalt_principles
concepts.definition: Wertheimer 1923. Proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, common fate, figure-ground. Perception organises features into wholes. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional concept emergence via shared neighbours.

concepts.name: top_down_perception
concepts.definition: Higher cortical predictions bias perception of ambiguous input. Helmholtz's unconscious inference, Gregory's hypothesis testing. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity field biasing basin selection in low-information input.

concepts.name: bayesian_perception
concepts.definition: Posterior P(world | input) ∝ P(input | world) × P(world). Knill + Pouget 2004. Cortex computes posterior over hypotheses. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity_field × external_field → posterior σ.

concepts.name: categorisation
concepts.definition: Sorting stimuli into classes. Rosch 1973: prototype theory + basic-level categories. Murphy 2002. Substrate analogue: substrate's concept-vs-Mt structure.

concepts.name: concept_formation
concepts.definition: Acquiring a new mental category. Empirical exemplars + abstraction. Substrate analogue: substrate's feature_invention process building new Concept nodes.

concepts.name: mental_imagery
concepts.definition: Internal representation of visual information without sensory input. Kosslyn 1980. Activates visual cortex similarly to perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime simulation via Term-tree evaluation without input events.

concepts.name: system_1_system_2
concepts.definition: Kahneman 2011. System 1: fast, automatic, intuitive, heuristic. System 2: slow, effortful, analytic, rule-based. Substrate analogue: System 1 = FilterSpec dispatch via runtime_discovery; System 2 = ArchitectureCortex deliberate assessment.

concepts.name: heuristic
concepts.definition: Mental shortcut. Availability, representativeness, anchoring (Tversky + Kahneman 1974). Fast but biased. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction shortcut bypassing full re-derivation.

concepts.name: cognitive_bias
concepts.definition: Systematic departures from rational norm. Confirmation bias, hindsight bias, availability heuristic. Kahneman + Tversky catalogued ~200. Substrate analogue: substrate's known failure modes in unchecked dynamics.

concepts.name: prospect_theory
concepts.definition: Kahneman + Tversky 1979. Decision-making under risk: loss aversion, reference-dependence, diminishing sensitivity, probability weighting. Won Nobel Prize. Substrate analogue: substrate's asymmetric weight on positive vs negative ΔF.

concepts.name: expertise
concepts.definition: Anderson + Schunn 2000. ~10 years deliberate practice. Domain-specific perceptual chunks (de Groot's chess masters). Substrate analogue: substrate's accumulated Mt structure in a domain — many fine-grained concepts.

concepts.name: transfer_of_learning
concepts.definition: Applying knowledge learned in one context to another. Near vs far transfer. Substrate analogue: substrate's analogical_transfer faculty + cross-Mt genlMt connections.

concepts.name: metacognition_psychological
concepts.definition: Flavell 1979. Thinking about thinking. Includes metamemory + metacomprehension. Substrate analogue: substrate's ArchitectureCortex assessing other cortices.

concepts.name: feeling_of_knowing
concepts.definition: Subjective awareness that you DO know something, even before retrieval. Hart 1965. Substrate analogue: substrate's predicted-success estimate before running ActionSpec.

rules.name: working_memory_capacity_constrains_processing
rules.head: the substrate must hold multiple items active at once
rules.body: performance degrades when the count exceeds ~4. Substrate's persistent-σ capacity has the same constraint.

rules.name: encoding_specificity_principle
rules.head: the substrate must retrieve a stored memory
rules.body: retrieval is best when the current σ pattern matches the σ pattern at encoding. Tulving 1973 — substrate's recall accuracy = match between current basin + stored basin.

rules.name: depth_of_processing_predicts_retention
rules.head: the substrate encodes a new concept
rules.body: deep integration into existing Mt structure produces better long-term retention than surface event-only encoding. Craik + Lockhart 1972.

rules.name: system_1_versus_system_2_dispatch
rules.head: the substrate decides how to handle an event
rules.body: if a relevant FilterSpec/ActionSpec exists (System 1), dispatch automatically; else escalate to ArchitectureCortex deliberation (System 2). Kahneman 2011.

rules.name: prospect_theory_asymmetric_weighting
rules.head: the substrate evaluates a gain vs loss of equal magnitude
rules.body: the loss feels ~2x more impactful. Substrate's negative ΔF triggers correction more strongly than equivalent positive ΔF triggers consolidation.

rules.name: expertise_through_chunking
rules.head: the substrate accumulates experience in a domain
rules.body: it develops domain-specific concept chunks that compress recurring patterns. de Groot 1946. Substrate's Mt enrichment over time.
